title: Fluorescent Biosensor Imaging of Nitrate in Arabidopsis thaliana
author: Yen-Ning Chen
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML
materials: Note: Constructs were inserted using an Entry clone by Gateway LR reactions into the yeast expression vectors pDRFlip
The NiMet3.0 is fused to the full-length of NasR with pDRFlip30 vector and sandwiched between an N-terminal Aphrodite t9 (AFPt

variant ( Deuschle et al., 2006 ), with nine amino acids truncated off the C terminus, and a C-terminal monomeric Cerulean (mCer) ( Rizzo et al., 2006 ). Note: The pDRFlip30 vector was modified from pDRFlip39 vector (Addgene, catalog number: 65517). Agrobacterium strain: Agrobacterium tumefaciens strain GV3101 was used here to obtain high transformation rates and high levels of expression, typically leading to high copy insertion into the genome ( Koncz and Schell, 1986 ). Arabidopsis thaliana: wild type Col-0, a nitrate transporter mutant [npf6.3/NTR1;1/chl1-5 (Leran et al., 2014)], and a nitrate reductase mutant [nia1nia2 ( Desikan et al., 2002 )] were used. steps.title: Prepare YPD medium
steps.instruction: Dissolve 10 g peptone (2 % w/v), 5 g yeast extract (1 % w/v) and 12 g agar (2.4 % w/v) in 500 mL distilled water, autoclave at 121 °C, 15 psi for 15 min; after cooling to hand‑warm temperature add 25 mL of 40 % sterile‑filtered glucose stock to obtain a final 2 % glucose concentration.

steps.title: Prepare solid –ura DropOut medium
steps.instruction: Combine 1.7 g yeast nitrogen base w/o amino acids w/o ammonium sulfate (1.7 g L⁻¹) and 0.77 g DO supplement‑Ura (0.77 g L⁻¹) in 1 L distilled water, adjust pH to 5.8 with NaOH, add 12 g agar (1 % w/v) before autoclaving at 121 °C, 15 psi for 15 min; after cooling add 50 mL of 40 % sterile‑filtered glucose stock to reach 2 % glucose.

steps.title: Prepare PLATE mixture for yeast transformation
steps.instruction: Make a 100 mL stock containing 90 mL 45 % PEG4000, 10 mL 1 M lithium acetate, 1 mL 1 M Tris‑Cl pH 7.5, and 0.2 mL 0.5 M EDTA. Mix well before use.

steps.title: Prepare wash buffer (MES 50 mM)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 9.76 g MES hydrate in 1 L distilled water, adjust pH to 5.5 with NaOH, autoclave at 121 °C, 15 psi for 15 min.

steps.title: Prepare resuspension buffer
steps.instruction: Mix 250 mL of the MES 50 mM buffer (Recipe 4) with 0.125 g agar (0.05 % w/v). Allow to cool to room temperature before use.

steps.title: Prepare plant growth solid base
steps.instruction: Dissolve 0.78 g half‑strength MS salts without nitrogen in 1 L distilled water, add 25 mL of 20 % sterile‑filtered sucrose stock to obtain 0.5 % sucrose (w/v), adjust pH to 5.5 with KOH, add 12 g Phytoagar (1 % w/v) before autoclaving at 121 °C, 15 psi for 15 min.

steps.title: Prepare nitrate substrate solutions
steps.instruction: Dissolve the desired amount of KNO₃ (or other substrate) in 50 mL MES buffer (50 mM) to obtain the required nitrate concentration; dilute with MES or MOPS buffer as needed for assays.

steps.title: Transform yeast with sensor plasmids
steps.instruction: Perform the modified lithium acetate transformation as follows:

substeps.instruction: Inoculate BJ5465 yeast in YPD medium and grow at 30 °C overnight to OD₆₀₀ ≈ 0.5.
Spin down 1 mL of culture at 2,000 × g for 15 s in a micro‑fuge tube; discard supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 100 µL YPD by vortexing.
Add 2 µL of 10 mg/mL carrier salmon‑sperm DNA; vortex.
Add ~1 µg of the sensor plasmid; vortex.
Add 0.5 mL of PLATE mixture; vortex.
Add 20 µL of 1 M DTT; vortex.
Incubate the mixture at 25 °C for 6–8 h (or overnight).
Heat‑shock at 42 °C for 10 min.
Using a pipette tip, withdraw 50–100 µL of the transformed cells and spread onto solid –ura DropOut plates.
Wrap plates with plastic cling wrap and incubate lid‑down at 30 °C for 2–3 days.

steps.title: Select and grow transformed yeast colonies
steps.instruction: Pick at least three independent colonies from the plates and inoculate each into 10 mL of liquid –ura DropOut medium (2 % glucose) in a 50 mL tube; incubate at 30 °C, 220 rpm for ~15 h until OD₆₀₀ ≈ 0.5.

steps.title: Subculture yeast to mid‑log phase
steps.instruction: Dilute each overnight culture to OD₆₀₀ = 0.01 in fresh liquid –ura DropOut medium; grow at 30 °C, 220 rpm until OD₆₀₀ ≈ 0.3.

steps.title: Harvest and wash yeast cells
steps.instruction: Collect cells by centrifugation at 3,000 × g for 10 min at room temperature; discard supernatant and resuspend in 10 mL wash buffer, vortex 15 s at RT; repeat centrifugation and wash two more times (total three washes).

steps.title: Resuspend cells for assay
steps.instruction: Resuspend the washed pellet in resuspension buffer and adjust to OD₆₀₀ ≈ 0.5.

steps.title: Set up fluorescence assay in 96‑well plate
steps.instruction: Aliquot 100 µL of the cell suspension into each well of a flat‑bottom 96‑well plate; add 100 µL of the appropriate nitrate substrate solution (or control) using a single‑ or multichannel pipette; mix by pipetting up and down; set up at least three replicates per treatment; record fluorescence immediately after addition.

steps.title: Measure fluorescence
steps.instruction: Using a plate reader in bottom‑reading mode with 7.5 nm bandwidth, record emission spectra: donor (mCer) λ_em 470–570 nm, step 5 nm, gain 75; acceptor (AFPt9) λ_em 520–570 nm, step 5 nm, gain 75. Excite mCer at λ_ex 428 nm and AFPt9 at λ_ex 500 nm. Reading of a full 96‑well plate takes ~10 min; for high accuracy read only a few wells at a time or use an injector‑type instrument.

steps.title: Prepare Agrobacterium culture with sensor plasmid
steps.instruction: Transform A. tumefaciens GV3101 with the sensor construct; then:

substeps.instruction: Inoculate a single transformed colony into 5 mL LB containing spectinomycin 100 µg/mL; grow overnight at 28 °C.
Next morning inoculate 200 mL LB with spectinomycin 100 µg/mL using the overnight culture; grow at 28 °C for 16–24 h.
Harvest cells by centrifugation at 3,000 × g for 10 min at RT; discard supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in an equal volume of freshly prepared dipping medium.
Adjust the suspension to 6 × 10⁹ cells mL⁻¹.

steps.title: Perform Arabidopsis floral dip
steps.instruction: Grow wild‑type Col‑0 (or mutant) Arabidopsis under 12 h light, 50 % humidity, 22 °C until flowering (3–4 weeks);

substeps.instruction: Remove siliques and mature flower clusters.
Spray the Agrobacterium suspension onto the floral parts.
Place dipped plants in a plastic basin, cover with plastic wrap for 16–24 h to maintain high humidity.
Remove the cover and grow plants normally for ~1 month; withhold watering when siliques turn brown.

steps.title: Select transgenic Arabidopsis
steps.instruction: Surface‑sterilize seeds and plate on 1/2× MS agar (with vitamins) containing kanamycin 30 mg L⁻¹; incubate under standard growth conditions and select resistant seedlings.

steps.title: Germinate transgenic seedlings for imaging
steps.instruction: Sow seeds on vertical plates containing 1/2× MS without nitrogen, 1 % agar, 0.05 % sucrose (w/v), pH 5.7; grow seedlings 5–6 days old.

steps.title: Prepare seedlings for confocal nitrate treatment
steps.instruction: Place a 5‑ or 6‑day seedling on a glass slide with 50 µL of 1/2× MS + 0.05 % sucrose (pH 5.7) solution; surround the droplet with a rectangle of vacuum grease; cover with a coverslip that matches the height and half the width of the grease rectangle; exchange nitrate solution beneath the coverslip by adding on the left side and removing on the right side as needed.

steps.title: Acquire confocal images of nitrate sensor
steps.instruction: Use a Zeiss LSM 780 (or equivalent) with either a 20×/0.8 Plan‑Apochromat dry or 40×/1.2 C‑Apochromat water objective. Excite CFP at 440 nm and YFP at 514 nm. Detect emission with a GaAsP PMT (463–508 nm for CFP) and a normal PMT (520–585 nm for YFP). Set laser power between 0.5 % and 2 %, detector gain 700–750. Acquire Z‑stacks with 1.5 µm step size, covering half the primary root diameter. Record time‑points as required (e.g., <1 h intervals for nitrate distribution studies).
